Commentary.Commentary: So, India landed the first punch in Manchester, England returned a mild one back in Cardiff and then the Men in Blue delivered the knockout blow here in Bristol. They take the 3-match T20I series 2-1 and will be full of confidence heading into the ODI series. The first match is on the 12th of July in Nottingham at 12.30 pm local (11.30 am GMT). Don't forget to join us. Until then, it's goodbye and cheers!

India captain, Virat Kohli says that the comeback from his bowlers was outstanding. Feels that a score of 225-230 was on the cards but he credits his bowlers for restricting England. States that his bowlers have good skills and they executed their plans to perfection. Adds that he is proud of his boys. Believes that Pandya is a very confident cricketer - both with bat and ball. Opines that the way he came back after being hit for 22 in the first over is what any captain would like to see. Adds that the all-rounder getting 33 in quick time was the icing on the cake. Backs his decision to not play Kuldeep Yadav as he feels that every bowler suffered here. Announces that they want to continue trying different things going ahead. Expresses that it is great to have a series win at the start of the tour and they will be aiming to build upon this.

England captain, Eoin Morgan says that it was a tremendous start with the bat. Appreciates Roy and Buttler for setting a great platform but rues the fact that the batsmen who followed couldn't capitalize. Credits India for bowling well. Opines that they were below par on a ground where the pitch was flat and the boundaries were short. Adds that it was a tough ground to defend on. (On the crowd supporting India) Morgan replies that teams like India and Pakistan have a huge fan following and the English team is used to it. Mentions that this series has had three different tests for them. Reckons that Trent Bridge (venue for the 1st ODI) has been a good ground for them. Reminds that they have lost a few tosses there in the recent past but the results have gone their way. Ends by saying that the toss will be less important and hopes it will be an entertaining contest.

Man of the Match and Series, Rohit Sharma says that assessing the conditions at the start was important. Mentions that once they saw off the new ball, they knew that the wicket was good and the boundaries were small. States that when he bats, he likes to take his time and not panic too much. Stresses the importance of spending time in the middle as it helps him to make up anytime during the innings. Also adds that it is crucial to assess the bowlers. Praises Hardik Pandya for his batting skills. Adds that he has played some good knocks when they really needed him to. Also credits him for his bowling and feels that he is a fearless individual.

When Hardik Pandya arrived at the crease, the tourists needed 48 off 31 balls. With Rohit Sharma at the other end batting on 83, the ball was still firmly in India's court. A quiet 16th over followed after Kohli's wicket but that didn't disturb India's progress much. Jake Ball went for 15 runs in the next over and that opened the floodgates. The Sharma-Pandya combo hammered the required runs with ease and achieved the target with 8 balls to spare. It was that kind of a day when you are not supposed to talk too much about the bowling unless the bowler's name is Hardik Pandya. He also started on a wrong note by conceding 22 in his first over but then in the next three overs, he picked up 4 wickets by giving away only 16 runs. The Indian all-rounder has warmed up well for this tour.

198 on any ground is a challenging total, even a match-winning one, but not here in Bristol where the boundaries are on the shorter side. India lost a couple of wickets inside the Powerplay but never compromised on the asking run-rate. Rohit Sharma held one end with all the class and elegance and along with his skipper Virat Kohli, he raised an 89-run stand off just 57 balls. England did manage to remove Kohli from the crease but failed to create a big enough opening to trouble the visiting team.

Where did England lose the match? Umm... From 103/1 in 9.1 overs to 198/9 in 20 overs. They fell short of a challenging total in spite of having a strong launching pad. Reminds me of a phrase - When you aim high, you set yourself up to fall far! The approach while batting for the Englishmen was to keep going for runs even if wickets were falling. Cannot fault them for doing so on a stamp size ground but then they should have planned it in a better manner. Also, one should give credit where it's due. The Indian bowlers, who were under the cosh after taking a hammering, showed a lot of character by bouncing back.

Emphatic win for India! Rohit Sharma was the architect of it as he stroked a magnificent century. Not to forget Hardik Pandya though. First, he did it with the ball by picking a 4-fer and then played a nice cameo to make India's path smooth to a series win. Clinical stuff from the Men in Blue.

SIX! Pandya has nailed it! Jordan serves a slower delivery again but lands it right in the hitting zone of Hardik Pandya. He just swings his bat and dismisses it over long on for a biggie. A 50-run stand in only 23 balls. INDIA WIN BY 7 WICKETS AND TAKE THE SERIES 2-1!
Slower in pace and outside off, punched down to covers.

HUNDRED FOR ROHIT SHARMA! His third in this format, only Colin Munro has these many in T20Is. A nice little dab to third man for a single to reach there. The Indian dugout is on its feet. Yet another scintillating knock by the Hitman!
FOUR! What a hit! An overpitched delivery outside off, Rohit takes the aerial route and drills it over covers for a boundary. Moves to 99!

FOUR! Width on offer outside off, Pandya stays back and just dabs it down to third man for a boundary. 20 from the over. India within a striking distance. Rohit also only 5 away from a century. 9 needed more for a win.

FOUR! A full toss this time, Pandya latches onto it and throws his bat at it. His bottom hand comes off the handle but he still manages to tonk it from the middle. It flies over cover-point and beats the dive of Stokes in the deep.

SIX! Into the crowd! This guy has all the range when it comes to playing big shots. Willey delivers it full and around off, Hardik gives it the full whack of his bat and sends it whistling over extra cover for a maximum.
It's been driven superbly through the covers. They pick up a single.
FOUR! Wonderful shot! Uses his crease superbly. It's fuller in length around off, Rohit shuffles across a bit and paddles it over backward square leg for a boundary. Nearly went all the way.
Fullish and outside off, driven through covers for a single.
David Willey returns for his final spell. India need 29 from 18. They will be backing themselves to chase this down but if they lose a wicket or two, who knows! The pressure might get to them.
Yorker outside off, dug out to third man for a run. 15 from the over. All the good work done in the previous two overs (where only 7 runs came) has gone down the drain.
The batsman guides it to third man. They pick up a single.

FOUR! Third boundary of the over. Short in length around off, Sharma pulls it off his front foot and places it nicely. Bisects the square leg fielder and the mid-wicket fielder to send it to the fence.
Taps it down to backward point for a single.

FOUR! And then he can do this as well. Placed his shot behind point. The length is altered by Ball. He goes very full and outside off, Hardik squeezes it out for a boundary. It is already looking like a great move to promote Hardik.
FOUR! Bang! Back of a length ball around off, Pandya shifts his weight sideways and smashes it over mid off for a boundary. He is an exceptional hitter of the cricket ball.
Jake Ball is back into the attack. 44 required off 24 balls.

Floated full ball on middle and leg, heaved away to deep mid-wicket for a run. Only 4 from the over, that brings an end to what has been a really good spell from Adil Rashid. He finishes with figures of 4-0-32-0. We can compare him with the Indian leggie, Chahal who had finished with figures of 4-0-30-0. Has been a decent day for the spinners.
Shorter in length, cut away with the spin to sweeper cover for a run.
Outside off, tapped towards short third man. Pandya wants a run but Rohit rightly sends him back.
Full and in line of the stumps, Pandya lofts it towards long on for a single.
Floated outside off, Pandya sees it through.
On a flatter trajectory outside off, Rohit punches it through covers to rotate strike.
Shortish outside off, played down to point. 3 from the over and a big wicket of Kohli. If England win this match, they will have to thank Jordan for this over.
Hardik Pandya gets a promotion. 48 needed off 31 balls.

OUT! Another sharp catch in the field. This time a return catch. Jordan takes it with ease. Mind you, that wasn't so easy. But then Chris is an exceptional fielder. Fuller and on off, 136 kph, Kohli hammers it straight back. It's uppish and Jordan gobbles it. End of an 89-run stand which has put India on the front foot. Can England still believe?
A low full toss on off, it's flicked to deep mid-wicket for a single.
Two dot balls now. Another mistimed drive by Rohit, this time he finds the extra cover fielder. So far so good by Chris.
Very full and around off, Rohit goes hard at it and mistimes his shot back to the bowler.
Slower delivery, short and around off, Kohli pulls it to deep mid-wicket for a single. 150 comes up for India, 49 more needed.
Wide! Jordan bowls it full and wide outside off, maybe just wide of the tramline. Kohli leaves it alone.

FOUR! 13 coming from this over. India are right on course. Plunkett offers room outside off and Sharma goes inside-out over covers. Not the best of connections but good enough to fetch him a one-bounce boundary.
Very full and on off, knocked down to long on for a single.
Too full and wide outside off, Rohit plays a lovely square drive and takes a single. Wants the second run as well but Kohli turns it down.
Fine leg comes up for Rohit Sharma.
Short in length and outside off, Kohli pulls and does well to keep it all along the ground through mid-wicket. A single taken.

SIX! Boom! For a moment, we thought Virat lost his balance but he kept his shape enough and sent it soaring over wide long off for a biggie. And once again, the white object has lost its shape. The umpires are getting it changed. 58 needed off 40 balls, that's the game situation.
Play and a miss! On a length and wide outside off, Kohli flashes and misses.
Liam Plunkett is back on.
SIX! A gift on the pads. Full toss. Rohit picks it up and deposits it over square leg for a biggie. Spoils what would have been a top over. 10 coming from it eventually.
Slower in pace and that deceives the batsman. Sharma swings his bat across the line but only manages a bottom edge back to the bowler.

Full toss on middle, it's lofted down the ground and it goes on one bounce to Stokes at long on. He nearly overran there. Only a single. The third umpire however was asked to check whether Ben touched the rope while in contact with the ball. Nothing like that on the replays though.
Shortish and on off, Sharma guides it down to third man for one.

Full and sliding down the leg side, Kohli clips it through mid-wicket and runs the first run hard. Bairstow in the deep senses that and charges towards the ball. He although returns a poor throw, it kept them down to only a run.
A low full toss outside off, Rohit reaches out for it and hits it towards point. Another good stop by Roy in that region but he can't prevent the single.
Chris Jordan is back on.
Gets back and strokes it with the turn to sweeper cover for one. 9 from this over, they are keeping the asking rate under check.
The batsman has flicked the ball off his pads. They pick up a single.
Turning back into the batsman from around off, Kohli rocks back and punches it to mid-wicket. Straight to the fielder.
SIX! High and handsome! Kohli gives the charge to the leggie and takes him head on. Makes excellent connection and dumps it over long on for a biggie.
Short and on middle and off, Kohli punches it off his back foot but finds the cover fielder.
Loopy full ball outside off, it's hit down to long on for a single.
Played to the mid-wicket region by the batsman. The batsmen have run through for a single. 16 from the over, 83 needed off 54 balls.

FOUR! Cheeky this time. A little bit of charge down the track and then he works a shortish ball fine. Deflects it off the outer half of the bat past the keeper for a boundary at third man. 50-run stand comes up.
SIX! That has gone a mile! Fourth biggie for Rohit. He gets a shortish ball around off and dispatches it with utter disdain over mid-wicket for a maximum.
A short delivery which has been pulled away. The batsmen have run through for a single.

Aerial but safe. Kohli mistimes his pull shot in the air and the fielder comes running in from the deep mid-wicket region. But it falls in front of him and then goes past him. By the time, the fielder collects it, they take a couple.
Angling down the leg side, nudged away to fine leg for a couple.
Liam Plunkett is back on.

Takes a step forward and then steers it with the spin to deep point. A couple to bring India's 100. It's from this stage England started to lose the plot. India will do themselves a favour by learning from that. The thing working for them here is that they have a target in front unlike England who had a target in their mind.
Flighted one outside off, Rohit tries to slog but misses.
A tossed up leg spinner outside off, Rohit taps it with gentle hands to backward point.
Drags his length back and bowls it on middle, Kohli pulls it to deep mid-wicket for a run.
Flighted and full outside off, driven through covers for a couple of runs.

FOUR! You can't afford to keep bowling short and wide to these batsmen. They will hit you to the fence 9 out of 10 times. In the last over, it was Rohit, this time it's Virat Kohli. He camps back and cuts it through point. There are a couple of fielders inside the ring for that shot but the skipper found the gap with ease.
Too full and on middle, it's been flicked to deep mid-wicket for a single.
Shortish and outside off, Rohit stays back and opens the face of his bat to play it past the diving point fielder for a single. Roy there got his hand to it but failed to stop it cleanly.
The batsman plays a pull shot to this short delivery. One run added to the total.
Slower one, full and wide outside off, Sharma slices his attempted cover drive and it goes on one bounce to the third man fielder. A single taken.

FOUR! Lucky way to get to his fifty! A good one though, off 28 balls only. Short and on middle and leg, Rohit fails to middle his pull shot properly and it loops wide of the keeper for a boundary. His 16th T20I half century. India need him to last the distance in this run chase.
Hits the yorker mark around off, Kohli squeezes it out to third man for a single.
Gets on the front foot and drives it square of the wicket on the off side for a single. The required run rate at the moment for India is 9.75. Need to keep going strong.
Played to the mid-wicket region by the batsman. One run added to the total.

FOUR! No stopping it this time. Adil Rashid got away with one at the start of this over but not this time. He bowls it flatter and shorter outside off, Rohit rocks back and delays his square cut a bit to get his placement right. No chance for the sweeper cover fielder this time.
Moves back to a shortish ball and punches it to deep cover for a single.
Presses forward to a full ball and drives it through covers for a run.
Starts with a flatter and shorter delivery outside off, Sharma cuts it firmly through point and Bairstow in the deep makes a tumbling stop. Saves two for his team.
Adil Rashid time.
Gets across the stumps to a length ball and flicks it straight to mid-wicket. Great over, just 2 runs off it.
Fuller and wider outside off, this time Rohit steers it past point for a single.
Gets bat on ball this time but finds the point fielder.
Too full and wide outside off, Sharma reaches out for it but fails to make any connection.
The batsman has pushed it to the cover region. One run added to the total.
Fullish and outside off, driven square of the wicket on the off side. Roy makes an outstanding stop at point.
Ben Stokes to bowl now.
Short and wide outside off, tapped down to third man for one. 70/2 in the Powerplay, going almost neck and neck with England at this stage. The hosts were 73/0 after 6.
FOUR! Those wrists of Kohli. You pay to watch him play that flick shot. Ball is too straight in line and the Indian skipper plays his bread and butter shot to put it away through mid-wicket.
Kohli opens the face of the bat and helps it to third man. They manage to come back for the second.
A length ball on middle, flicked through mid-wicket for a single.
Virat Kohli arrives at number 4. 137 needed off 88 balls.

OUT! Another cracking catch to dismiss an Indian batsman. Chris Jordan this time who went for 16 in his first over has taken a brilliant running cum diving catch. Take a bow. Ball gets a wicket, he was involved in the first wicket as well. Probably an off-paced delivery, on a length and around middle, Rahul aims to go downtown and clear long on. But he ends up getting a lot of height than distance. Jordon first backtracks from mid on and then hares across to his right, covers a lot of ground before diving to take a ripper of a catch. Kept his eyes glued to the ball like a hawk eyes his prey. KL departs without doing much damage.
SIX! Shot! Back of a length ball just around off, Rahul picks it up from there, turns inside the crease and dismisses it over backward square leg for a maximum.
Jake Ball returns.
Gets behind the line and pushes it back past the bowler for a run at mid on.

SIX! It has gone all the way! Brings up 50 for India. Not sure Rahul intended it to go there but he won't be complaining. Good length ball around off, Rahul tries to play the inside-out shot over covers but ends up slicing it over third man for a maximum.
Shortish and wide outside off, Rahul rocks back to play the square cut but mistimes it towards the point fielder.
Plunkett bowls it full and on middle, Sharma leans forward and across before flicking it through mid-wicket for a single.
FOUR! Rohit is motoring. Receives a length ball around off, spots the room to lift it over covers and does so with aplomb. Good enough connection to take it across the fence.
Fair start as long as you are not conceding a boundary first ball. Width on offer outside off. Rahul slashes it down to third man for a single.
It's Liam Plunkett's turn, to pick a wicket or to take a hammering, not sure.
Angles it into the batsman, not enough room and Rohit defends it back. 16 from the over.

SIX! Pulled it and pulled it beautifully. He is one of India's best batsmen when it comes to pull a cricket ball. Jordan drops it short and Rohit shows no mercy. Swivels inside the crease and pulls it over fine leg. Into the crowd.
It seems the ball has lost its shape after the last hit. The umpires get together and are getting it changed. Something similar happened when England were batting also.
SIX! Rohit was waiting! He was waiting for the bowler to pitch it full and in his half. As soon as Jordan commits that sin, Sharma lines himself up and pumps it over long on for a biggie.
Good length ball on middle, defended on the leg side.
Another free flowing drive from the bat of Rohit but this time Willey does extremely well at covers to stop the racing ball.

FOUR! 2000 T20I runs for Rohit Sharma, becoming the third Indian after Mithali Raj and Virat Kohli to reach this feat. Jordan delivers it full and wide outside off, Sharma cracks his drive through covers and finds the fence.
Chris Jordan is into the attack.
On the pads of Rohit who flicks it through mid-wicket for a single.
Fuller and straighter, knocked towards the deepish mid on fielder for one.
Back of a length ball on off, played down square of the field on the off side. Finds point.
This one is angled across the batsman, KL pushes it off his front foot to covers.
FOUR! Shot of a batsman in prime form. An overpitched delivery alright, around middle, Rahul strides forward and creams his straight drive down the ground for a boundary.
KL Rahul is the number 3 batsman.

OUT! Stunner by Ball! You need to take catches like these to stay in hunt on an unforgiving ground like this. Willey comes up with a delivery in the line of the stumps, Dhawan tries to flick it away across the line but fails to keep it down. It flies towards short fine leg where Ball quickly reacts to his left and hangs on to a sharp catch. Dhawan cannot believe his luck. Shakes his head in disbelief and has a wry smile on his face as he walks back. England are delighted.

FOUR! Smart batting! Rohit exposes all his stumps by moving down the leg side and Ball follows him with a full ball. The bowler is caught unaware that the fine leg is up inside the circle and there is a deep mid-wicket in place. Sharma calmly flicks it off his pads through square leg for a boundary.
Shortish and on middle, Dhawan stays back and taps it down in front of backward point for one.
Attempts the slower one this time but the line is a little too straight, Rohit clips it in front of square leg and crosses.
These are nice lines. Bangs it in, around middle and off, Rohit remains back in defense.
Better line and length. Just behind a good length around off, Rohit punches it off his back foot to covers.

FOUR! No bowler will be spared today, if he fails to get his length right. Ball drops the ball short and on middle and leg, Rohit rides the bounce and eases it with the pull shot behind square leg for a boundary.
Jake Ball will share the new ball from the other end.

FOUR! Exquisite! That will be great for Dhawan's confidence. Full length ball outside off, Dhawan leans ahead a touch and drives it crisply through covers to find the fence. Good start for India, 11 from the first over.
Fullish ball close to the off stump, Sharma plays it with soft hands to mid-wicket to rotate strike.
In the zone outside off, Rohit doesn't fiddle with it.

SIX! What a shot! The good thing is that Sharma didn't get rattled after the first two good deliveries. He walks down the track and clips the fullish ball nonchalantly over cow corner to clear the ropes.
This is brilliant thinking from Willey! After swinging one in, he bowls this one on a length and the ball seams away after landing. Sharma has a tame push at it and misses.

Some action straightaway! Full length ball on middle, swinging in the air. Sharma tries to flick it away but misses to get hit on the pads. Willey is confident but the umpire stays put. The replay shows that it was probably going down leg.

A great comeback in the last 5 overs by the Indian bowlers and now it's up to their batsmen to carry the momentum forward. Out come the dangerous duo, Rohit Sharma and Shikhar Dhawan to open the batting. David Willey to start off the proceedings with the ball. Here we go...
